mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary regime that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced household income expectations, lowering equity demand and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes despite GDPC1 falling by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase above 0.4 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which erode corporate earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months when UNRATE rises by more than 0.4pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes despite INDPRO falling by more than 0.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) and Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals improved household balance sheets and stronger housing demand, which boosts consumer confidence and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA and RSAFS > 12-month MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) and the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.3% month-over-month indicates a coordinated easing of inflation and policy rates, which lowers risk premia and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered months when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS fall by more than 0.3% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes despite PAYEMS exceeding 100,000 for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual decline in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (GDPC1) below -1% for two consecutive years signals secular demand weakness, which erodes corporate revenue growth and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, regardless of the monetary policy stance.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -1% for two consecutive years
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes despite GDPC1 falling by more than 1% annually for two consecutive years.
